chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Battat narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

He said: The greedy man is deprived of two characteristics, and two characteristics become attached to him: He is deprived of contentment, so he lacks comfort; and he is deprived of satisfaction (with God's decree), so he lacks certitude.

key_terms.حَرِيص: Greedy person / One who is eager for more

ai.seo_question: What are the two characteristics a greedy person is deprived of and what do they lose?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the dialectic of loss and burden in spiritual psychology, where greed (hirs) actively strips the soul of tranquility and certainty while imposing the weight of dissatisfaction. This reflects the Shia ethical emphasis on internal states (ahwal) as indicators of faith, linking the absence of contentment directly to a fragility in theological conviction. The narration serves as a diagnostic tool for self-reflection, urging believers to cultivate qanā'ah as a prerequisite for stable yaqīn.
